ip_top_stories.title: Round Hill Files $1 Billion Copyright Infringement Suits Against Suno, Anthropic
ip_top_stories.summary: Music rights company Round Hill has filed copyright infringement lawsuits against AI companies Suno and Anthropic, with claims potentially reaching $1 billion. The suits relate to the alleged unlicensed use of copyrighted music for AI training purposes. This represents one of the largest copyright actions yet brought against AI developers by music rights holders.

ip_top_stories.title: ByteDance Inks Copyright Deal With Motion Picture Association Over AI Video Tools
ip_top_stories.summary: TikTok parent ByteDance has reached a copyright agreement with the Motion Picture Association (MPA), establishing AI copyright safeguards relating to ByteDance's AI video generation tools. The deal follows a dispute between ByteDance and Hollywood studios over AI-generated video and IP rights. It is one of the first formal licensing-style agreements between a major AI company and a major entertainment industry trade body.

ip_top_stories.title: Record Labels Can Pursue Piracy Claim Against AI Song Generator
ip_top_stories.summary: A court has ruled that record labels may proceed with a piracy claim against an AI song generator, marking a significant development in music copyright litigation involving AI tools. The decision allows the case to move forward, potentially setting precedent for how existing copyright law applies to AI-generated music. Details of the specific AI company involved were not provided in the article headline.

ip_top_stories.title: Japan to require AI firms to disclose training data
ip_top_stories.summary: Japan's government is urging AI companies to disclose the data used to train their models, as part of efforts to combat IP infringement. The move signals a policy shift toward greater transparency in AI development and reflects growing international concern about unlicensed use of copyrighted material. Japan has previously taken a relatively permissive stance on AI training data under its copyright law.

ip_top_stories.title: South Korea Opens the Door to Copyright Registration of AI-Assisted Works
ip_top_stories.summary: South Korea has moved to allow copyright registration of works that are AI-assisted, marking a notable shift in how the country's legal framework treats human-AI collaborative creative output. The development positions South Korea among a small number of jurisdictions beginning to formally address the copyright status of AI-generated or AI-assisted content. The policy details and scope of human contribution required for registration eligibility were not fully specified in the article.

ip_further_links.title: Naver's pre-ChatGPT AI disclosures disputed in South Korean copyright trial
ip_further_links.summary: A South Korean copyright trial involving Naver has seen disputes over the AI disclosures the company made before ChatGPT's rise, raising questions about what AI training practices were declared and when.

ip_further_links.title: German court says AI comic based on dog photo did not violate copyright
ip_further_links.summary: A German court has ruled that an AI-generated comic derived from a photograph of a dog did not constitute copyright infringement, offering a significant data point in European courts' emerging approach to AI and image copyright.

ip_further_links.title: Book Publishing Is Being Flooded by AI – and Nobody Knows What to Do
ip_further_links.summary: A broad look at how AI-generated content is proliferating across book publishing, with industry stakeholders uncertain how to respond to the scale and pace of AI-authored submissions and publications.

ip_further_links.title: AI Invades Religion Books on Amazon [Metered]
ip_further_links.summary: A study has found that 63% of religion books on Amazon are likely AI-written, highlighting the scale of AI-generated content flooding one of the platform's major categories.

ip_further_links.title: Guest Post — AI Can Find the Article. Can It Tell Which Version It Used?
ip_further_links.summary: A Scholarly Kitchen guest post explores the challenge of AI systems being unable to reliably identify which version of a scholarly article they have used, raising questions for academic publishing and citation integrity.

ip_further_links.title: AI Music Is Growing, But Is India's Copyright Law Ready?
ip_further_links.summary: An analysis of whether India's existing copyright framework is equipped to handle the rapid growth of AI-generated music and the IP questions it raises.

ip_further_links.title: The Patent Litigation Review 2027 - Philippines: inventorship and patentability of AI-assisted inventions
ip_further_links.summary: A review of how the Philippines is approaching questions of inventorship and patentability in the context of AI-assisted inventions, as part of a broader international patent litigation survey.
